data.narrative:
Quantum Motion is a Series C quantum computing startup founded by John Morton and Simon Benjamin. The company has raised $160M+ to date. The quantum computing sector includes 3 public comparables (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private peers including Quantinuum, IonQ, PsiQuantum, D-Wave Quantum, and SandboxAQ.

A single valuation method is applicable to this analysis. Stage-progression methodology uses the $160M total raised as a baseline proxy for current valuation and applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C to later-stage transitions, yielding an implied valuation of $272M. Peer-median comparison cannot be reliably applied: while 8 same-sector private competitors exist, insufficient datapoints meet narrow filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation-tier comparables (fewer than 3 required), and using all-sector median would introduce misleading noise rather than directional signal.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $231M (low) to $313M (high), with $272M as the median. Given reliance on a single method, key uncertainties include: the appropriateness of the 1.7x multiplier for Quantum Motion's specific capital efficiency and milestone trajectory; the absence of narrow peer benchmarking to validate market pricing; and execution risk inherent to early-stage quantum hardware development. A broader peer dataset or additional internal milestone milestones would strengthen conviction in this range.
